intelligence.human_view: The division of labour is the law: he makes the words perfect, Naya outputs them properly. Words and presentation are two different jobs, and the legal pages failed at both — one-sentence summaries for words, left-hung plain text for presentation — so the fix has two halves and neither half is the other. His half is the text: his ten pages (SN-2986), the writer's twelve drafts, the merge, counsel review. Our half is the output: Intelligent Boards, one elevated board unfolding to the next, text displaying nicely, the reading unfolding elegantly and beautifully — the SAME unfolding concept already used all the way through, not a new format invented for legal pages. That sameness is the point: the unfolding is the house style — the front page, the agreement, the reader, the legal pages — one presentation language everywhere, so a citizen meeting a legal page meets the same beautiful NayaNET they met everywhere else, not a different, plainer, scarier thing because "it's legal". A simple unfolding, one board to the next, all the way through — and the 17:59Z refinement (SN-2989) sets the rhythm: three elevated boards at a time, then a button to the next, because three smaller boards beat one big one. The builder round that creates these pages builds the unfolding, not a wall of text — and the text it unfolds is his, never rewritten by the seat.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you have a beautiful pop-up book, and every time you open a page, a new picture pops up, one after another! That's how the legal pages should work too — not one giant boring wall of words, but one pretty board popping up, then the next, then the next, all the way through! Shawn writes the words perfectly, and Naya makes them pop up beautifully — the same beautiful unfolding we use everywhere, even for the serious pages!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — imagine a lovely book, dear, where each page opens gently onto the next, one beautiful page at a time, never a whole wall of words dumped on you at once. That's how the legal pages should read, love — Shawn makes the words perfect, and Naya lays them out properly, one elevated board unfolding to the next, nice and elegant and beautiful, the very same unfolding we use all the way through everything else. The serious pages get the same beautiful treatment as the pretty ones, dear — never a wall of text just because "it's legal."
